title: Abstract Base Classes & Protocols
html:
Two ways to describe “what an object must be able to do”: ABCs check it by inheritance (nominal typing), Protocols by shape (structural typing — static duck typing).

abc.ABC and @abstractmethod

An abstract base class can't be instantiated while it has abstract methods. Subclasses must implement every one of them — the error appears when you create an object, not when you call the missing method.

Abstract properties & class methods

Key point

An abstract method may still have a body; subclasses can call it with super().method() — handy for shared default behaviour that must be consciously opted into.

collections.abc: get methods for free

The ABCs in collections.abc are mixins: implement the few abstract methods and inherit the rest. Implement __getitem__ + __len__ and Sequence gives you in, iteration, reversed, index and count.

isinstance with ABCs, register & __subclasshook__

Some ABCs (Sized, Iterable, Hashable, Callable…) check structurally through __subclasshook__: any class with the right method counts. You can also declare a virtual subclass with register.

Watch out

register is a promise, not a check — Python never verifies that the registered class really implements the methods.

typing.Protocol — structural typing

A Protocol lists the methods a type needs. Any class with those methods matches — no inheritance, no registration. Type checkers (mypy, pyright) verify it statically; @runtime_checkable also enables isinstance.

Watch out

A runtime isinstance check against a Protocol only checks that the method names exist — not their signatures or return types. Signature checking happens only in the type checker.

ABC or Protocol?

ABC (abc.ABC)Protocol (typing.Protocol)
Typing styleNominal — must inherit or registerStructural — just have the methods
EnforcedAt instantiation (TypeError)By the static type checker
Shared codeYes — concrete methods, template methodsPossible, but only for explicit subclasses
Works with third-party classesOnly via registerAutomatically
Best forFrameworks and class hierarchies you ownLibrary APIs, callbacks, “anything with .read()”
Do

Use an ABC when you own the hierarchy and want to share implementation; use a Protocol to describe what a function accepts from arbitrary callers.

Avoid

Creating an ABC for every class “just in case” — in Python, plain duck typing is often enough.

Interview angle

Why can't you instantiate a class with abstract methods?

ABCMeta records unimplemented @abstractmethods in __abstractmethods__; object.__new__ refuses to create an instance while that set is non-empty. The subclass becomes concrete once it overrides all of them.

Nominal vs structural typing?

Nominal: a type matches only if it declares the relationship (inherits from the ABC). Structural: a type matches if it has the required members (Protocol). Python's runtime is duck-typed; Protocols bring that duck typing to static type checkers.

What does collections.abc give you beyond isinstance checks?

Mixin methods. Subclass Sequence, Mapping or MutableSet, implement the handful of abstract methods, and you inherit a full, consistent API — the safe way to build a custom container instead of subclassing list or dict directly.
